P3:03_rod_cloud.style: HOS cream-on-brown period-paper inked mechanism diagram, Didot italic
P3:03_rod_cloud.label: DRAWING CHARGE FROM CLOUD
elements: Inked stone tower elevation with sentry-box and pointed iron rod rising toward passing storm cloud
Animated dotted charge lines curving down from cloud base into the sharp rod tip

P3:15_wet_dry.style: HOS cream-on-brown period-paper inked mechanism diagram, Didot italic
P3:15_wet_dry.label: WET TWINE · DRY SILK
elements: Inked vertical wet hemp twine carrying animated charge dashes down to the iron key
Dry silk ribbon tied below the key where charge dashes halt at the insulator knot
P3:15_wet_dry.animation: Twine, iron key and silk ribbon ink in by 0.8 s; animated charge dashes flow down the wet twine into the key (1.0–3.0 s) and stop cleanly at the dry silk boundary (3.0–5.3 s).

elements: Left moving pane: Leyden jar spark in back room (P2:08_jar_spark)

P4:08_teach_charge.style: HOS cream-on-brown period-paper inked mechanism diagram, Didot italic
P4:08_teach_charge.label: NO BOLT, JUST CHARGE
elements: Inked storm cloud high at top of period sheet, silk kite flying well below in rain
Gentle dotted charge lines draining quietly down the wet string to the shed key without any bolt
P4:08_teach_charge.animation: Cloud, kite and shed silhouette ink in over 0.0–1.2 s; soft dotted charge lines flow steadily down the string from 1.2 s to 7.1 s; label NO BOLT, JUST CHARGE inks in at 0.6 s and fades out at 4.4 s.

P5:08_looking_path.style: HOS inked stepped-leader diagram composited over moving storm-rooftop plate (alternates with P5:09 full-frame card)
P5:08_looking_path.label: EASIEST PATH DOWN
elements: Branching ink leader lines feeling downward from cloud base toward town roof peaks over moving storm plate
P5:08_looking_path.animation: Forked ink leader paths draw downward step by step from 0.3 s to 2.8 s over the moving rooftop plate, testing paths toward the highest gable.

P5:09_wood_vs_metal.style: HOS cream-on-brown period-paper inked cross-section diagram, Didot italic
P5:09_wood_vs_metal.label: WOOD AND STONE RESIST
elements: Inked cross-section of timber roof rafters and stone steeple masonry with jagged fracture lines where current is blocked
P5:09_wood_vs_metal.animation: Timber roof and stone steeple outlines ink in over 0.0–1.2 s; blocked current path marks resistance points at 1.8 s and radial crack lines draw outward across the masonry through 6.8 s.

P5:10_metal_easy.style: HOS inked conductor diagram composited over moving Set H brick-wall rod plate (alternates between P5:09 and P5:11 full-frame cards)

P5:10_metal_easy.label: METAL CONDUCTS
elements: Smooth gold-and-white inked current line running unimpeded down the iron rod on the moving brick wall plate
P5:10_metal_easy.animation: Inked callout bracket marks the iron rod at 0.25 s; a smooth continuous current trace glides straight down the rod from top to bottom over 0.4–2.8 s.

P5:11_safe_path.style: HOS cream-on-brown period-paper architectural cutaway diagram, Didot italic
P5:11_safe_path.label: SAFE PATH DOWN
elements: Cutaway elevation of church steeple fitted with pointed iron rod, exterior down-conductor wire, and deep earth stake
Animated current line travelling from rod tip down the outside wall into the ground while interior timber spire stays untouched
P5:11_safe_path.animation: Steeple cutaway and exterior iron rod ink in over 0.0–1.3 s; current line traces from rod tip down the outer wall into the earth stake (1.5–6.5 s); label SAFE PATH DOWN inks in at 0.6 s and fades out at 4.4 s.
